title: Moral luck
summary: Same choice, same intentions — but only one driver hits someone.
intro: Two people make the exact same decision, with the exact same information and intentions. Only luck decides what happens next. Does the outcome change how much blame they deserve?

questions.prompt: Two people drive home drunk, taking the identical risk. One makes it home; the other hits and kills a pedestrian who stepped out unexpectedly.
questions.scenario: Judge them for what they did, not what happened after.

options.label: They deserve the same blame — the decision was identical
The one who killed someone deserves more blame

questions.prompt: Two people plan and attempt the same robbery with a loaded gun. One's gun jams; no one is hurt. The other's fires, killing the shopkeeper.

options.label: The one who killed deserves a harsher punishment

questions.prompt: Two surgeons make the identical small technical error in similar operations. One patient recovers fine. The other develops a rare complication and dies.

options.label: Review both identically — the skill and care were the same
The surgeon whose patient died should face more serious consequences

questions.prompt: Two people text while driving through the same empty stretch of road for the same ten seconds. One arrives home; a child runs into the road in front of the other.

options.label: The one involved in the accident bears more responsibility

questions.prompt: In general, how much should the outcome — not just the intention and the risk taken — affect how we judge someone?
questions.minLabel: Judge the decision, not the result
